newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products - Gasolines sluggish from bull run.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products - Gasolines sluggish from bull run.

text.p: U.S. cash gasoline differentials were stable to slightly weaker in late Monday trade that was sluggish throughout the day after last week's bullish move in the U.S. Gulf Coast.
The stability lasted despite the sharp early decline on NYMEX futures, which fell after U.N. officials in Baghad approved Iraq's aid distribution plan.
The approval brings Iraqi oil sales nearer to a restart date.
NYMEX August futures ended 0.91 cent down to 58.35 cents a gallon and August heating oil closed off 0.68 cent at 51.67 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF
Gulf Coast gasoline markets were decidedly tough to peg Monday after last Friday's action that saw strength in "M1" regular unleaded grade spread up to the NYMEX in New York.

"It's really kind of flaky today," said one gasoline trader in Houston, who pegged prompt M1 for delivery in time for Colonial Pipeline's front 21st scheduling cycle on Thursday at between 0.50 and 0.15 cent under August NYMEX unleaded.
That was considerably weaker than on Friday, but a touch firmer than earlier Monday.
"It started out today all offers and no bids, and now it seems like all bids and no offers," said the trader.

Also, prompt front 21st cycle "M2"-grade regular conventional, a grade sold in much of the northern tier of the U.S., traded in Houston at 1.00 cent under August NYMEX after trading at 1.25 cent under in the early going.
Distillates meanwhile remained dormant at least differentially speaking.
"I don't think differentials have changed much in two months," a Gulf Coast distillate trader said.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Regular conventional "M2"-grade gasoline weakened modestly as ample supplies pressured differentials, according to market watchers.
Nearby conventional barrels dipped to about 2.50 cents under the August futures, a loss of about 0.50 cent from late Friday levels.
"There's some gasoline cargoes available in the Harbor, some Venezuelan, European and Argentine stuff," one player said, though most of the barrels available probably require further refining.
Prompt reformulated "A2"-grade gasoline also weakened, with offers sitting near 0.75 cent over the August futures.
Premium reformulated gasoline remained in short supply, according to traders, lifting differentials early in the day as a prompt parcel traded at 8.75 cents over the August futures.
MIDCONTINENT

Gasoline differentials in the Midcontinent remained largely steady after a brief sell-off this morning lowered values. The sell-off was spurred by a decline in U.S. Gulf Coast differentials and a drop in NYMEX futures following the Iraqi news.
In Group Three, prompt unleaded gasoline differentials were pegged 2.75/3.25 cents in thin talk, down a quarter cent from Friday. Any month barrels were also steady at 2.25/2.50 cents over the print.
"It's very quiet this afternoon and many people are watching the Merc," said a gasoline trader.

In Chicago, prompt unleaded gasoline differentials were unchanged at 2.25/2.65 cents over the print. Any month barrels were 1.35/1.75 cents, after a deal done earlier this morning at 1.75 cents. Differentials were down by 0.10 to 0.25 cents from Friday.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
